title: ONO-03 · Names of places and entities

blocks.text: ONO-03 · Names of places and entities
Lesson overview

After the names in person (ONO-01) and their Latin spellings (ONO-02), the track of names passes to the names of places and bodies. Casablanca is ⁧الدَّارُ البَيْضَاءُ⁩ , Tangier is Tanger in French and ⁧طَنْجَة⁩ in Arabic, Damascus is also ⁧الشَّام⁩ ; the Arab Republic of Egypt is listed in the addresses as ⁧ج.م.ع⁩ ; UNESCO is ⁧اليُونِسْكُو⁩ but also the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization. In this unit you learn to recognize the place names in their variants, to break down the long names of the institutions, to dissolve acronyms and abbreviations and to read an Arabic address. They are reading and transcription skills, useful to anyone working with documents, news and public sources. Two weeks.

rows: ONO-01, ONO-02, A2-09 (entities and offices); form B1.2 exceeded
10–12 hours · two weeks (weeks 124–125), plus the EGY track

blocks.text: Materials This unit, an atlas or an online map in Arabic, voice synthesis scripts, tutor session
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. recognizing the Arab names of countries, with and without article, in the short form and in the official form;
2. link Arabic toponyms to their Italian, French and English forms, and vice versa;
3. recognizing frequent geographical elements in place names ( ⁧بِئْر⁩ , ⁧عَيْن⁩ , ⁧وَادٍ⁩ , ⁧جَبَل⁩ , ⁧رَأْس⁩ , ⁧تَلّ⁩ …);
4. break down and translate long names of international ministries, bodies and organisations;
5. loosen the most common abbreviations ( ⁧ج.م.ع⁩ , ⁧ص.ب⁩ ., ⁧د⁩ ., ⁧م⁩ ., ⁧ق.م⁩ .);
6. read and write an Arabic address.
Two-week plan.

1. Dialogue 1 · Tanger, Tangier, Ṭanǧa
At the police station. Karīm, the interpreter of Fès, helps Luca to read a list of Moroccan cities written French.

rows: ⁧لُوكَا⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم، هٰذِهِ القَائِمَةُ مَكْتُوبَةٌ بِالفَرَنْسِيَّةِ:⁩ “Tanger, Oujda, Ksar el-Kébir”. ⁧كَيْفَ تُكْتَبُ بِالعَرَبِيَّةِ؟⁩
Luca: Karīm, this list is written in French: "Tanger, Oujda, Ksar el-Kébir" . How do they write in Arabic?
⁧كَرِيم:⁩ Tanger ⁧هِيَ طَنْجَة، بِالطَّاءِ. وَ⁩ Oujda ⁧هِيَ وَجْدَة: الـ⁩ • • • ⁧الفَرَنْسِيَّةُ وَاوٌ.⁩
Karīm: “Tanger” is Ṭanǧa, with ṭāʾ. E .Oujda is Waǧda: the French "ou" is a wāw.
⁧كَرِيم⁩ : ⁧القَصْرُ الكَبِيرُ.⁩ Ksar ⁧هِيَ⁩ « ⁧قَصْر⁩ » ⁧، وَلٰكِنْ فِي المَغْرِبِ نَنْطِقُهَا بِلَا⁩ ⁧حَرَكَةٍ بَعْدَ القَافِ.⁩
Karīm: Al-Qaṣr al-Kabīr. Ksar isqaṣrIn Morocco we pronounce it without voice after the qāf.
Got it. And "Casablanca"? It's not an Arabic word!
⁧وَبِالعَرَبِيَّةِ⁩ .« ⁧البَيْتُ الأَبْيَضُ⁩ » ⁧صَحِيحٌ، هِيَ إِسْبَانِيَّةٌ، وَمَعْنَاهَا⁩ : ⁧كَرِيم⁩ ⁧نَقُولُ: الدَّارُ البَيْضَاءُ. التَّرْجَمَةُ نَفْسُهَا!⁩
Karīm: Right, it's Spanish and it means white house. In Arabic we say ad-Dār al-Bayḍāʾ: the same thing translated!

⁧كَرِيم⁩ : ⁧كِلَاهُمَا! الفَرَنْسِيُّونَ يَكْتُبُونَ⁩ • Fès ⁧، وَالإِنْجِلِيزُ⁩ • Fez ⁧، وَنَحْنُ نَكْتُبُ⁩ ⁧فَاس. وَلَا تَنْسَ: فِي المَغْرِبِ تُكْتَبُ الأَسْمَاءُ فِي الوَثَائِقِ الرَّسْمِيَّةِ بِالعَرَبِيَّةِ⁩ ⁧وَبِالحُرُوفِ اللَّاتِينِيَّةِ مَعًا.⁩
Karīm: Both of you! The French write "Fès" , the English "Fez" , and we write Fās. And don't forget: in Morocco, in official documents, names are written in Arabic and Latin characters together.
⁧إِذَنْ لِكُلِّ مَدِينَةٍ ثَلَاثَةُ أَسْمَاءٍ عَلَى الأَقَلِّ!⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩
Luke: Then every city has at least three names!
Karīm: And sometimes four: the inhabitants of Damascus also call their cityaš-Šām»!

blocks.text: What to notice. ⁧طَنْجَة⁩ : the French T's hides a ṭāʾ. ⁧وَجْدَة⁩ : “ou” = ⁧و⁩ (ONO-02). ⁧القَصْرُ الكَبِيرُ⁩ : Ksar is attached to the adjective with the article in Arabic the article is on both words. ⁧الدَّارُ البَيْضَاءُ⁩ : a translated toponym, not transliterated. ⁧فَاس⁩ / Fès / Fez: three graphs, one city. ⁧الشَّام⁩ : Traditional name of Damascus and, in the broad sense, of historical Syria (the Levant). ⁧القَائِمَة⁩ The list is given in the table below. ⁧نَنْطِقُ⁩ We're pronouncing. ⁧كِلَاهُمَا⁩ Both of them. ⁧الوَثَائِق⁩ • documents (pl. of ⁧وَثِيقَة⁩ ). ⁧الحُرُوفُ اللَّاتِينِيَّةُ⁩ The Latin characters are the same as the Latin characters.
2. Exonyms and endomins

An endemic name is the name of a place in the language of those who live there ( ⁧القَاهِرَة⁩ ); An exonymous name is used by other languages (Cairo, Le Caire, Cairo). Three or four forms usually coexist for Arabic places:
⁧القَاهِرَة⁩ al-Qāhira Cairo Le Cairo Cairo

Two traps. 1. ⁧الجَزَائِر⁩ is both the capital and the country: the context decides. 2. ⁧طَرَابُلُس⁩ indicates two cities, in Libya and Lebanon; when it is necessary to specify: ⁧طَرَابُلُسُ الغَرْبِ⁩ (Libya), ⁧طَرَابُلُسُ الشَّامِ⁩ / ⁧طَرَابُلُسُ لُبْنَانَ.⁩
3. Names of countries
With or without article. Some country names always have the article, others never: it has to be learned by name.

· ⁧البَحْرَيْن⁩ · ⁧الكُوَيْت⁩ · ⁧المَغْرِب⁩ · ⁧اليَمَن⁩ · ⁧السُّودَان⁩ · ⁧الأُرْدُنّ⁩ · ⁧العِرَاق⁩ · ⁧عُمَان⁩ · ⁧قَطَر⁩ · ⁧لِيبِيَا⁩ · ⁧تُونُس⁩ · ⁧لُبْنَان⁩ · ⁧سُورِيَا⁩ · ⁧مِصْر الإِمَارَات⁩ · ⁧السُّعُودِيَّة⁩ · ⁧الجَزَائِر⁩ ⁧مُورِيتَانِيَا⁩ · ⁧فِلَسْطِين⁩
The official name. In documents, treaties and official titles the long name appears:

The pattern. Type of State ( ⁧جُمْهُورِيَّة⁩ , ⁧مَمْلَكَة⁩ , ⁧سَلْطَنَة⁩ , ⁧دَوْلَة⁩ , ⁧إِمَارَة⁩ ) + name in iḍāfa ( ⁧جُمْهُورِيَّةُ مِصْرَ⁩ ) or + nationality adjective ( ⁧المَمْلَكَةُ المَغْرِبِيَّةُ⁩ ). The subdivisions. Arab countries use different names for their regions: ⁧مُحَافَظَة⁩ in Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Iraq; ⁧وِلَايَة⁩ in Algeria, Tunisia, Sudan; ⁧جِهَة⁩ / ⁧إِقْلِيم⁩ in Morocco; ⁧إِمَارَة⁩ in the Emirates; ⁧مِنْطَقَة⁩ Saudi Arabia. In Italian, they usually translate with "governorato" , "provincia" , "regione" .
4. Elements of the place names
Many place names are common words with a transparent meaning. Recognizing them helps to rebuild Arabic spelling:

Structure. It's almost always aiḍāfa: element + name ( ⁧بِئْرُ السَّبْعِ⁩ The seven-fold well, or name + adjective ( ⁧القَصْرُ الكَبِيرُ⁩ The great castle). In Latin writing the article becomes el, al, es-, ez-... (Deir ez-Zor = ⁧دَيْرُ الزُّورِ⁩ , with assimilation).
5. Latin graphs of the place names
The rules of ONO-02, with a few more habits:
Egyptian pronunciation Giza = ⁧الجِيزَة⁩ · Port Said = ⁧بُورْسَعِيد⁩ · Mansoura = ⁧المَنْصُورَة⁩

rows: Deir ez-Zor = ⁧دَيْرُ الزُّورِ⁩ · Ras el-Ain = ⁧رَأْسُ العَيْنِ⁩
Casablanca = ⁧الدَّارُ البَيْضَاءُ⁩ · Port Said = ⁧بُورْسَعِيد⁩ (port of Saʿīd)

blocks.text: The method. As for the names of person: island consonants, recognize tradition (ou, ch, dj → French; sh, j → English; g → Egypt), look for a known item (Bir, Ain, Ras...), and check on a map in Arabic or on an encyclopedia.

Nādya translates a statement into Arabic in English and asks Luke for help with the names of the institutions.

Nādya: Luca, do you know the Arabic name of ...

⁧، أَوِ الاِسْمَ الكَامِلَ: مُنَظَّمَةُ الأُمَمِ المُتَّحِدَةِ⁩ « ⁧اليُونِسْكُو⁩ » ⁧يَقُولُونَ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧لِلتَّرْبِيَةِ وَالعِلْمِ وَالثَّقَافَةِ.⁩

⁧نَادْيَا⁩ : ⁧وَهُنَا:⁩ : Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics. ⁧هٰذَا مِصْرِيٌّ.⁩
Nādya: And here: Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics. This is Egyptian.
⁧الجِهَازُ المَرْكَزِيُّ لِلتَّعْبِئَةِ العَامَّةِ وَالإِحْصَاءِ. مَعْرُوفٌ بِاسْمِ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧فَقَط، أَوْ بِالاِخْتِصَارِ الإِنْجِلِيزِيِّ.⁩ « ⁧الجِهَازِ⁩ »

7. Names of institutions: how they are built
An entity name reads from left to right in English and from right to left in Arabic, but the logic is the same: type of entity + scope + adjectives.

rows: type + scope + adjective of the institution
United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees

blocks.text: type + own name ⁧مَكْتَبَةُ الإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّةِ⁩ · ⁧جَامِعَةُ القَاهِرَةِ⁩ University of Cairo · Library of Alexandria

To whom does the adjective refer? It is the difficult point: in long names the final adjective may refer to the first name ( ⁧مُنَظَّمَةُ الصِّحَّةِ العَالَمِيَّةُ⁩ : is the organization to be world-wide) or at last ( ⁧وِزَارَةُ التَّعْلِيمِ العَالِي⁩ : education is higher). Watch genre and chance when there are vowels, otherwise the meaning and official name. Frequent international organizations.
8. Symbols and abbreviations
Arabic uses a few initials, and often points. The most common in documents:
⁧م.⁩ ⁧مُهَنْدِس⁩ Engineer (title, Egypt)

Foreign acronyms are transcribed and read as words: ⁧اليُونِسْكُو⁩ , ⁧الفِيفَا⁩ , ⁧النَّاتُو⁩ . They often appear with the article. ⁧م⁩ . ambiguous. ⁧م⁩ . can be 'engineer' before a name ( ⁧م. أَحْمَد عَلِيّ⁩ ) or (d.C.) after a date ( ⁧٢٠٢٦م⁩ ). The context decides.
9. Addresses

An Arabic address often goes from small to large, as in English: name, building, street, neighborhood, city, village. In Egypt and the Levant, civic numbers and postal codes are used less than in Europe; often give reference points ( ⁧أَمَامَ⁩ , ⁧بِجِوَارِ⁩ , ⁧خَلْفَ⁩ ).
⁧ج.م.ع.⁩ – ⁧القَاهِرَةالزَّمَالِك⁩ – ⁧١٥ شَارِعُ مُحَمَّد مَظْهَرالطَّابِقُ الثَّالِثُ⁩ – ⁧مَعْهَدُ اللُّغَاتِمَارْكُو فِيرَّارِي⁩ / ⁧السَّيِّدُ⁩
Note. The address and recipient of the example are invented. ⁧السَّيِّدُ⁩ / is the opening formula of Egyptian addresses (with the bar).
10. Pronunciation

Toponimi with assimilated article. ad-Dār al-BayḍāʾDayr az-Zūr, Šarm aš-Šayḫ: solar letters assimilate the article in their own names. Read the long names. munaẓẓamatu ṣ-ṣiḥḥati l-ʿālamiyya: read in one breath, with the desinences ofiḍāfa; in pause the last word loses the vowel. The French spellings out loud. The tutor reads a French spelling (Oujda, Tétouan, Chefchaouen); You pronounce her in Arabic.
11. New lexicon

Notes of use. ⁧جِهَاز⁩ is the apparatus ( ⁧جِهَازُ كُمْبْيُوتَرٍ⁩ ) but also the State body: in the names of institutions it translates with "Institute" , "Agency" , "Ente" . ⁧كِلَا⁩ / ⁧كِلْتَا⁩ want the name to the dual in iḍāfa: ⁧كِلَا البَلَدَيْنِ⁩ • both countries • • • with a pronoun they decline: ⁧كِلَاهُمَا⁩ (No.), ⁧كِلَيْهِمَا⁩ (Ac., Jan.).

14. Reading
Reading · A city, many names (partly vocalized)
